newsitem.title: USA: Coal makes an investment comeback -- Barron's.
newsitem.headline: Coal makes an investment comeback -- Barron's.

text.p: An increase in productivity in the coal industry as well as a trend towards consolidation is good news for investors in coal companies, according to Barron's business weekly.

The article said on Sunday companies like Zeigler Coal Holding Co stand to benefit from the consolidation trend within the industry, where hundreds of small operators have closed or sold their mines in recent years.

Also, the deregulation of the electric utility industry is a plus for coal companies like Zeigler and Ashland Coal Inc. As competition increases among utilities, low-cost coal will be the fuel of choice for many electric power plants, Barron's said.
Zeigler's chief executive, Chand Vyas, told Barron's the utilities' demand for coal could lift coal sales 20 percent to 25 percent above the current annual volume within a decade.
Besides Zeigler and Ashland, Barron's said Cyprus Amax Minerals Co and Pittston Minerals Group are in good positions, though both these companies mine other substances as well.
